name: Nelson Mandela
role: South African anti-apartheid leader, ANC president and first democratically elected president of South Africa (1994-1999)
summary: Mandela was an African nationalist and democrat who held that apartheid had to be replaced by a non-racial, universal-franchise democracy. He accepted limited armed struggle from 1961 once peaceful protest was barred, then led negotiations and reconciliation, and as president ran a government of national unity with a mixed market economy. He admired parliamentary democracy and entrenched rights, and in his later years he campaigned on HIV/AIDS treatment and nuclear disarmament and criticised unilateral Western military action.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His government introduced free care for children under six and pregnant women in 1994, extended it to all primary public care in 1996; in 2002 he urged that everyone needing AIDS treatment get access.

public-ownership.rationale: Argued in 1964 for nationalising mines, banks and monopoly industry within a private-enterprise economy, but in office pursued privatisation and no nationalisation; the later record wins.

unions-good.rationale: Called organised labour an important partner crucial to reconstruction and condemned the denial of union recognition and collective bargaining to African workers; the 1996 Constitution protects unions and strikes.

cut-welfare.rationale: His government raised welfare spending in 1996-99 and equalised grants across races; he preferred jobs to handouts for the unemployed but did not seek cuts.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The 1996 Constitution adopted under his presidency excludes advocacy of racial, ethnic, gender or religious hatred that incites harm from free-expression protection.

state-harmful.rationale: Led a government he described as serving a people-centred society and expanding freedom, and set out the state's duties in the Reconstruction and Development Programme.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Called for restructuring the economy so apartheid's inequalities are addressed, backed black economic empowerment and deracialising the economy; the Constitution allows measures for the disadvantaged and restitution for land dispossession after 1913.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Urged the UN to reform itself and act decisively on conflicts, and in 2003 said he would back any action the UN agreed on while accusing Bush and Blair of undermining it.

free-trade.rationale: Announced a policy of systematically opening the economy to global competition within GATT commitments, in a carefully managed process.

nation-first.rationale: Told the UN that the world is an interdependent whole and no people is truly prosperous while others suffer; he pressed for cooperation, debt cancellation and aid rather than narrow national interest.

limit-growth.rationale: His government's plan called for a strong, growing economy with high sustainable growth, while keeping an environment ministry; no call to cap growth.

revolution-justified.rationale: Said that after peaceful protest failed he helped found MK and listed open revolution among the options to be held in reserve, civil war being a last resort; in 1990 he reaffirmed armed struggle as defensive until talks became possible.

central-planning.rationale: In 1964 stated that the ANC never advocated revolutionary change of the economic structure and that nationalisation would sit within a private-enterprise economy; his 1994-99 government ran a mixed market economy under GEAR.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: said unemployment should be fought 'not by way of handouts but by the creation of work opportunities', which points away from an unconditional income for all.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Chose to open the economy to global competition and to pursue trade agreements with the EU and US rather than shelter domestic industry.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Kept Chris Stals as Reserve Bank governor and said the Bank's task is to protect the currency and relative price stability.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rejected rule by a single party: led a Government of National Unity with the National Party and Inkatha, and the Constitution requires a multi-party system.

democracy-best.rationale: Called for universal suffrage in a democratic non-racial South Africa, and abided by majority decisions even when he disagreed.

workers-councils.rationale: Said he admired the parliamentary system and regarded the British Parliament as the most democratic institution in the world, unlike the Marxist view he described.

right-to-secede.rationale: Demanded a democratic, non-racial and unitary South Africa and worked to bring secessionist groups into the electoral process.

political-violence-never.rationale: Planned sabotage and led MK, saying violence became unavoidable when peaceful means were barred, and in 1990 called the armed struggle a defensive action.

war-builds-character.rationale: At the UN he called for defeating 'the glorification of arms, the adulation of force' and condemned resolving disputes by war.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Praised the independence of courts and judiciary and described the security forces as the state's defenders; no sign of privatised justice or defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Built his politics on non-racialism and a rainbow nation; rejected both white and black domination.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Praised those who acted 'without seeking selfish gain' and warned that indifference, cynicism or selfishness must not defeat humanism.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said he would tie himself to no system except socialism and would borrow the best from West and East, judging his political formula impartially.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Stated in 1964 that the ANC had never condemned capitalist society and sought to harmonise class distinctions rather than emphasise them.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Admired parliamentary democracy, called the ANC a 'parliament of the African people' and backed multiparty democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Said the Freedom Charter called for land redistribution but not nationalisation, and that Africans want to own land where they work.

taxation-theft.rationale: Governed with taxes funding the RDP, and said a permanently higher level of taxation was to be avoided rather than taxation rejected.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Called the vote the central demand: 'above all, we want equal political rights'.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Described white supremacy's notion of black inferiority as a legislated falsehood and said all people are born equal.

total-state.rationale: Pledged an entrenched human-rights culture and drew on civil society and organised labour, stating government must not be isolated from the people.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Told the UN to defeat the glorification of arms and to settle conflicts peacefully; urged withdrawal from East Timor.

bound-labor.rationale: Likened labour tenants on white farms to medieval serfs; his government's Land Reform (Labour Tenants) Act of 1996 protected tenants from eviction.

universal-morality.rationale: Told the UN that happiness, justice, human dignity, peace and prosperity have universal application because each people and individual is entitled to them.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred: called at the UN for respect for the independence and security of all States of the Middle East alongside Palestinian aspirations, which includes Israel as a state; he also criticised Israeli policy.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Announced a plan to contain real government consumption, manage the deficit 'with a view to its continuous reduction' and avoid permanently higher taxes.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backed the right of colonised peoples to control their own destiny and sought settlements in Western Sahara and East Timor meeting the interests of the peoples concerned.

force-without-un.rationale: In 2003 said he would support any action agreed by the UN against Iraq but attacked the US and UK for undermining the UN; opposed NATO's 1999 Kosovo intervention.

class-collaboration.rationale: Said the ANC seeks to harmonise class distinctions and committed his government to tripartite cooperation of state, labour and capital.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said women must be empowered 'as equals' in all aspects of life and that freedom requires their emancipation from all forms of oppression.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposed apartheid's segregation, passes and colour bars as the core injustice and fought for a non-racial democracy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Said freedom cannot be achieved unless women are emancipated from all forms of oppression and pledged to end gender discrimination.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Committed government to freedom from want, hunger and ignorance, funding housing, health care, water and education.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Condemned apartheid's separation of races and committed to a society where black and white live together in harmony.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said all people are born equal and entitled in equal measure to life, liberty, prosperity and human rights.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The 1996 Constitution adopted under his presidency guarantees everyone freedom of conscience, religion, thought and belief.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Cited the principle that 'the will of the people shall be the basis of authority of the Government' and said the apartheid state lacked African consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Insisted on one non-racial nation for all South Africans and condemned forced removals under apartheid.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Planned sabotage of property as a political tactic, though he called it defensive and tried to avoid loss of life.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rejected a system that made each person 'a predator whose survival depended on the destruction of the other', and stressed solidarity among peoples.

separated-powers.rationale: Praised the US doctrine of separation of powers and independent judiciary, and the Constitution he oversaw sets checks on political power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Described the ANC as an inclusive 'parliament of the African people' and said it was open to debate whether the Communist Party had a specific role.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said the government owed a commitment 'to the poor, the oppressed, the wretched' and made the RDP's goals central.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Objected that African strikes were illegal and union recognition denied; the 1996 Constitution protects the right to strike.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Attributed African poverty to apartheid legislation, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Championed a 'rainbow nation' and used the 1995 Rugby World Cup to bring communities together.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred: demanded in 1990 the immediate end of the State of Emergency as a precondition for negotiations, opposing emergency powers against opponents.

party-controls-media.rationale: The 1996 Constitution under his presidency guarantees freedom of the press and other media.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Called himself a loyal and disciplined ANC member bound by its democratic structures and abided by majority decisions he disagreed with.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The 1996 Constitution under his presidency protects freedom of artistic creativity.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Never planned a second term; retired in 1999 under a Constitution that allows two terms.

death-penalty.rationale: Said in 1964 that death sentences cannot cure social ills; his government kept the death penalty abolished and the Constitution guarantees the right to life.

minority-language-support.rationale: The 1996 Constitution recognises eleven official languages, requires state measures to elevate indigenous languages and sets up a board to protect other languages.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Listed debt cancellation among measures needed to help countries of the South.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said repealing racial laws would be hollow while the mines were owned by one race, and in 1990 called for fundamental restructuring of the economic system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Stated in 1990 that the country's future must be decided by a body democratically elected on a non-racial basis.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Told the UN that the divide between wealth and poverty must be addressed, including capital inflows, debt cancellation and technology transfers.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Pressed nuclear-armed states to eliminate their arsenals, asking why they need them at all.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Said the Reserve Bank's primary function is price stability and kept its governor, Stals.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Privately urged Suharto to withdraw from East Timor in 1997 and wanted a settlement meeting the interests of all peoples concerned.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Admired an independent, impartial judiciary and the supremacy of law; the 1996 Constitution binds the state to the rule of law.

land-redistribution.rationale: Said the Freedom Charter calls for redistribution of land; his government's constitution provides for restitution or redress for dispossession since 1913.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Backed black economic empowerment, and the Constitution allows measures to advance those disadvantaged by unfair discrimination.

delink-world-market.rationale: Described re-entering the global economy as a major challenge and sought foreign investment, trade talks and global competition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Called for an end to racism in the workplace; the Constitution bars unfair discrimination by private persons as well as the state.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Said he venerated the Bill of Rights and Magna Carta, and as president led adoption of a Constitution with an entrenched Bill of Rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Became the first president by election of the National Assembly and held that authority rests on the will of the people.

minority-veto.rationale: Abided by majority decisions and negotiated a power-sharing government rather than granting any minority a veto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Called the British Parliament the most democratic institution in the world.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Said he dedicated his life to the struggle and, even in retirement, stayed active in public affairs.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Told the UN that wealth accumulating in one part of the world generates poverty elsewhere, and called for the South to gain access to productive resources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Welcomed foreign funds and investment for the RDP and pressed rich countries for capital inflows.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Stated he fought against both white and black domination and sought equal political rights for all.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Said the government would create an attractive climate for foreign direct investment.

single-official-language.rationale: The 1996 Constitution adopted under his presidency gives eleven official languages parity of esteem.

non-intervention.rationale: Called for sanctions on Nigeria's junta and sought the international isolation of apartheid, and mediated in Burundi and Zaire.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The 1996 Constitution adopted under his presidency gives everyone a right of access to information.

informal-organisation.rationale: Described the ANC as a mass political organisation and a 'parliament of the African people', and sought legal organised mass action.

defeat-communism.rationale: Said communists were allies, saluted the SACP in 1990, and rejected the argument that cooperating with them made him a communist tool.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: referred at the UN to the defeat of 'the Nazi and fascist crime against humanity', treating Nazi crimes as established fact.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The 1996 Constitution adopted under his presidency bars unfair discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Led a power-sharing government and demanded free political activity for all organisations.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The 1996 Constitution under his presidency guarantees freedom of conscience, religion and opinion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Called the end of white minority rule a close to five hundred years of African colonisation and opposed colonial rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Pledged to bring civil society, labour and civic organisations into decision-making and to build communities' capacity to manage their affairs.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Held that the authority of government rests on the will of the people.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combined private-sector growth and market opening with fiscal discipline, consumer protection, labour partnership and social programmes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Called on security forces to defend sovereignty and security, and sought only elimination of nuclear weapons at the UN.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As president chaired the Non-Aligned Movement and was a proud member state of it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: His government adopted the market-oriented GEAR plan in line with World Bank and IMF thinking, while he urged reform of those institutions.

property-franchise.rationale: Demanded universal suffrage on a common voters' roll.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Admired judicial independence and the rule of law, which the Constitution makes a founding value.

racial-franchise.rationale: Demanded universal suffrage on a common roll in a non-racial democracy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argued that monopoly ownership by one race would perpetuate domination despite political power, and that accumulating wealth was generating poverty globally.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Backed the security forces and the criminal justice system, with juvenile detention reform and alternative care for children.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Led the 1994 Government of National Unity including the National Party and Inkatha.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Said the RDP was driven by solidarity rather than charity and funded it through the state budget.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Said he created MK to defend the people against force and called armed struggle a purely defensive action.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Saluted fallen MK combatants who paid the ultimate price and dedicated his inauguration to those who gave their lives.

second-chamber.rationale: Opened his government in 1994 by addressing the National Assembly and the Senate, the two-chamber Parliament he led under the interim constitution.

family-wage.rationale: Said Africans want to earn enough to support their families properly and be paid a living wage.

person-over-state.rationale: Said legitimacy rests on serving a people-centred society of individual freedom and dignity.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rejected organising politics by race, saying political divisions based on colour are artificial.

communal-electorates.rationale: Demanded a common voters' roll for all citizens.

future-generations.rationale: Said the environment ministry should secure a healthy environmental future 'even for generations not yet born'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Urged nuclear states to commit to the total elimination of nuclear weapons and condemned adulation of force.

capital-controls.rationale: Said exchange controls and the dual currency would be subjected to critical scrutiny as normality returns.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Complained that Africans were denied collective bargaining and pledged tripartite labour law reform.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Told the UN that multilateral financial and economic institutions must be restructured to serve the needs of the world's poor.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Took state power through elections and a Government of National Unity, working through existing institutions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Spoke of 'the common humanity that bonds both black and white into one human race'.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Urged the nuclear-weapons states to eliminate their weapons, calling arguments for keeping them naive.

women-suffrage.rationale: Demanded universal suffrage and equal participation of women in all aspects of public life.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Announced the statutory Gender Commission and organs of government to integrate women's emancipation.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Held that security forces serve a democratic system; the Constitution guarantees the right to life and bars torture.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Insisted leaders be democratically elected by their organisations and worked through party, parliament and civil society.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Led the Defiance Campaign of deliberate peaceful defiance of apartheid laws, saying acceptance would have meant being silenced.

multipolar-world.rationale: Criticised the primacy of some states over others and chaired the Non-Aligned Movement.

notes: Views changed over time. In 1964 he defended nationalising mines, banks and monopoly industry within a private-enterprise economy and said he was attracted to a classless society; in office (1994-99) his government pursued the RDP and then the market-oriented GEAR, with privatisation and no nationalisation, so the later record is used. In 1961-90 he defended armed struggle as a last resort; from 1990 he pursued negotiation and reconciliation. Answers resting on the 1996 Constitution reflect a text drafted by the Constitutional Assembly and adopted under his presidency, so they are medium confidence unless he also said the same himself. Nothing was taken from his party or label alone; items marked 'Inferred:' follow from a specific statement.
